dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: ...Aria, Canon.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: This was far beyond mere punishment — and not for the first time, either.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Be it the city of dragons our King entrusted to us, or the fragile yet beautiful homes built by those tiny humans...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: How many more innocent lives must you watch die before you stop standing idly by?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: If our King were still here—

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: He is not here, Sonnet.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: If that far-from-omnipotent ruler believes this pale, horrifying fate to be "order," if this is the only way to save this doomed world from being devoured, then...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: No matter how heavy the price demanded... and no matter how much sorrow that price brings me, it is far better than pitch-black silence.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: If the world is destined for destruction... What's the point of fighting the darkness?

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: ...Sonnet?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Nothing, Sister Aria! Forget I said anything at all!

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: I just think we shouldn't stand by and watch as that tyrant slaughters the living beings who put their faith in us... whether they be dragons or those tiny humans.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Shouldn't we... save them?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...I can understand Sonnet's anger, Aria. To me, what that ruler did was far too cruel.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Even if there's only the slightest chance... I want to do everything in my power to save those who can be saved.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: But... what about those who can't be saved?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Those for whom salvation does not come, whose lives were lost... Are their blood, tears, and wails of agony simply meant to vanish without a trace?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: No... That isn't how it should be. I wish for everyone to be saved, and for none to fall.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: If its "order" would perish alongside it...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: ...Sonnet. Do not forget the reason for our birth.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Our mission is solely to preserve this world until our King, who granted us life, returns from afar.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: We knew what this order would cost from the beginning... but we could not allow this world to march toward destruction.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...No, this isn't even about order, Aria.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Sonnet, to us... to me, you are our dearest little sister.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: So... please do not do anything that would hurt Aria and I.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Do not directly defy this heavenly order. At least... not now, while the world is still so fragile.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Canon... I...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Istaroth told me of a word that only humans may lay claim to... "hope."

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: As long as there is life, there is hope... There will always be hope.
